summary:
Project Roshni is an astronaut and habitat health-monitoring web application created by Team Roshni (Minahil Noor, Alishba Noor, and Sidrat-ul-Muntaha) from Mazen School, Islamabad, for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge. Built to protect crews during deep-space missions, it addresses NASA’s five core spaceflight hazards: radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, altered gravity, and hostile closed environments.

The software combines real-time biometric telemetry, daily self-check questionnaires, medical hardware diagnostics, and spacecraft/base environmental monitoring to catch health issues early. During emergencies, it provides non-doctor crewmates with simplified, step-by-step recovery guides—enabling autonomous care when communication delays prevent real-time support from Earth.

Powered by open-source NASA Space Apps datasets, the team built and launched the platform using Google Gemini (research and prompt engineering), Google AI Studio (frontend interface), GitHub (version control), and Netlify (cloud deployment)—showcasing how young innovators can create practical, life-sustaining tools for future space exploration.
details:
Project Roshni (ASTRO-CARE) is an astronaut and space-habitat health-monitoring web application created by Team Roshni (Minahil Noor, Alishba Noor, and Sidrat-ul-Muntaha) from Mazen School, Islamabad, for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge. It serves as an integrated medical command center designed to protect deep-space crews on spacecraft and lunar or Martian bases.

How It Works

The app protects crews against NASA’s five major spaceflight hazards (radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, altered gravity, and hostile closed environments) through four core features:

  • Automated Vitals: Tracks real-time heart rate, oxygen levels, and radiation exposure.
  • Daily Self-Checks: Logs subjective symptoms like mood, sleep quality, fatigue, and dizziness.
  • Medical Hardware Diagnostics: Schedules routine onboard cardiovascular, muscular, and neurological checks.
  • Habitat Integration & Emergency Triage: Links crew vitals to cabin air, pressure, and solar storm sensors, automatically launching simplified, step-by-step recovery guides when thresholds are breached.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Autonomous Care: Empowers crews to handle medical emergencies independently when deep-space communication delays (up to 20+ minutes) prevent live support from Earth.
  • Non-Doctor Friendly: Translates complex aerospace medicine into clear, jargon-free action cards so any crewmate can act fast under pressure.
  • Proactive Prevention: Catches compounding health and environmental issues early, making future Artemis lunar and Mars missions safer while showcasing student-led innovation using open NASA data.

Tools & Technologies Used

  • Data & AI: NASA Space Apps datasets and Google Gemini for medical research, workflow structuring, and prompt engineering.
  • Development & Deployment: Built with Google AI Studio (HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript), version-controlled on GitHub, and deployed live via Netlify.
  • Hardware: Built on student laptops as a lightweight, browser-based interface for spacecraft tablets and mission terminals.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

Team Roshni uniquely connected astronaut symptoms directly to habitat conditions (e.g., linking fatigue to cabin CO2CO_2CO2​ or radiation spikes). They designed the interface specifically to reduce cognitive load during emergencies, factor in limited onboard medical supplies, and normalize mental health tracking during long-duration isolation.
